newsitem.title: CANADA: Bloc Quebecois confident of Quebec sovereignty.
newsitem.headline: Bloc Quebecois confident of Quebec sovereignty.

text.p: The Bloc Quebecois will not need to fight another federal election because Quebec separatists will win the next referendum on the province's independence, party leader Gilles Duceppe said on Tuesday.
"The next referendum will be a winning one, so there will be no other elections for the Bloc," Duceppe told reporters.
Quebec's separatist Parti Quebecois government is expected to hold another referendum if it wins the next provincial election, which must be held by 1999.

The separatist Bloc won 44 seats of Quebec's 75 seats on about 38 percent of the French-speaking province's vote in Canada's election on Monday, down from 54 seats in 1993 on 49.3 percent of the vote.
Duceppe said the Bloc had difficulty getting its campaign under way, but that Quebec voters sent mainly sovereigntists to Ottawa.
"At the end of the line, 60 percent of the districts were won in Quebec, a majority of sovereigntist districts," Duceppe said.
But the Bloc was ousted as Canada's official opposition by the right-wing, Western Canada-based Reform Party.
Duceppe said Canada was "unreformable" and that there was no national consensus among the four other parties on the question of Quebec's constitutional demands.
"The reform of Canada for Canadians remains as impossible as the realization of Quebec's aspirations for Quebeckers," Duceppe said.
Duceppe accused Reform of being "anti-Quebec" and its leader Preston Manning of denying the existence of the "Quebec people."
